key: A WhatsApp group admin vote that needs a majority
name: ch09_admin_vote_majority
alt: Groups of three and five members still reach a majority with some phones offline, while a group whose admin has patchy signal keeps re-voting and gets nothing done.
scene: A split illustration of a WhatsApp-style group admin vote, drawn as people holding big phones. LEFT half, two small groups stacked one above the other. Top row: three friends in a circle, two holding phones with green tick vote bubbles and the third asleep on a charpai with his phone dark and a little moon above it; a tally shows two out of three, enough, with a green tick. Bottom row: five friends, two of them offline (one on a train in a tunnel, one in a cinema with the phone switched off), and the other three still raising green ticks, again enough. Beside them, a four-person row where one is offline and a fourth chair has just been added, the tally still needing three, shown with an equals sign to the three-person row. RIGHT half: the group admin, a young man in a hoodie on a rooftop holding his phone up to a weak signal with one flickering bar, rain clouds overhead. Around him the other members keep throwing paper ballots into a ballot box again and again, a circular arrow looping around the box, a pile of crumpled ballots on the floor and a wall calendar with every day marked only as an election day. A to-do list pinned to the wall stays untouched, with not one item ticked. The members look tired and annoyed, one yawning, one face-palming. Bright daylight on the left, grey drizzle on the right. Labels: "MAJORITY" at the top of the left half, and "RE-ELECTING" above the looping ballot box on the right.
